title: Human gut microbes impact host serum metabolome and insulin sensitivity
claim: P. copri was one of the species driving an association between microbial branched-chain amino-acid synthesis and insulin resistance. Giving P. copri to mice worsened glucose tolerance and insulin resistance.
studyType: Human observational study plus mouse experiments
limitation: Human association does not establish causation. A genus-level Prevotella measurement cannot identify P. copri or its metabolic genes; mouse effects do not establish a treatment effect in people.

title: Dietary Fiber-Induced Improvement in Glucose Metabolism Is Associated with Increased Abundance of Prevotella
claim: After a short barley-bread intervention, participants whose glucose metabolism improved had more P. copri and a higher Prevotella-to-Bacteroides ratio. This illustrates how associations can depend on dietary context.
scope: Genus ratio and species-specific P. copri findings
studyType: Human dietary intervention with mouse microbiota-transfer experiments
population: Healthy adults consuming barley-kernel bread for three days; germ-free mice
limitation: Short intervention and responder comparison. The study does not show that increasing every Prevotella species improves insulin sensitivity, or that this pattern applies to the iPOP cohort.

title: Oral administration of Blautia wexlerae ameliorates obesity and type 2 diabetes via metabolic remodeling of the gut microbiota
claim: Blautia, especially B. wexlerae, was less abundant in association with obesity and type 2 diabetes in Japanese adults. B. wexlerae administration improved metabolic outcomes in high-fat-diet mice.
studyType: Human cross-sectional study plus mouse experiments
population: Japanese adults; mice fed a high-fat diet
limitation: Human findings are observational, and the intervention was in mice. A Blautia genus abundance cannot establish that B. wexlerae is present or justify probiotic advice.

title: Gut microbial carbohydrate metabolism contributes to insulin resistance
claim: A microbial group containing Blautia and Dorea was examined in relation to insulin resistance and excess fecal carbohydrates, illustrating a different context from the B. wexlerae findings.
studyType: Human observational multi-omics study with bacterial culture and mouse experiments
population: 306 adults recruited at health check-ups; diagnosed diabetes was excluded
limitation: Community-level associations cannot assign the same function to all Blautia species or establish that changing Blautia alone would alter a person's insulin sensitivity.

title: Ruminococcus bromii is a keystone species for the degradation of resistant starch in the human colon
claim: R. bromii breaks down resistant starch and can make starch-derived nutrients available to other gut bacteria in culture, offering a possible dietary-function context for this genus.
studyType: Bacterial culture and human fecal-community experiments
population: Human gut bacterial isolates and fecal communities
limitation: This is functional biology, not evidence that Ruminococcus abundance predicts or treats insulin resistance. Genus abundance does not identify R. bromii or measure starch fermentation.

title: Eight-week exercise training in humans with obesity: Marked improvements in insulin sensitivity and modest changes in gut microbiome
claim: An eight-week exercise intervention improved insulin sensitivity and was accompanied by an increase in the Ruminococcus gauvreauii group, which correlated with the insulin-sensitivity measure.
scope: Ruminococcus gauvreauii group, as reported by the study
limitation: Exercise has many effects; correlated microbial changes do not establish mediation. This small study's taxonomic group should not be equated with every feature labeled Ruminococcus.

title: Gut microbial carbohydrate metabolism contributes to insulin resistance
claim: A. indistinctus consumed several carbohydrates in culture. Administering it to high-fat-diet mice reduced intestinal monosaccharides and improved insulin-resistance-related outcomes.
studyType: Human observational multi-omics study with bacterial culture and mouse experiments
population: Adults without diagnosed diabetes; bacterial cultures and high-fat-diet mice
limitation: The intervention evidence is preclinical. An Alistipes genus measurement cannot establish the presence or activity of A. indistinctus or predict a benefit in patients.
